# Pagination: `jl-pagination`

Moves through pages of results, with the current page, its neighbours and the ends a click away.

- Class `JlPagination`, a molecule: `import { JlPagination } from '@syware/jlib';`
- On the site: https://bioleyl.github.io/jlib/components/pagination

Moves through pages of results. It shows the first and last pages (boundaries), the current page with
siblings on each side, and a gap for the pages between; the number of buttons stays the same on every page, so they
do not jump under the pointer.

compact keeps only the arrows and "3 of 12", for a card or a phone. Listen to change for the page people go to; set
page from code when the results move for another reason.

## Use

```ts
import { JlPagination } from '@syware/jlib';
```

```tsx
<JlPagination page={6} pages={12} />
```

```html
<jl-pagination page="6" pages="12"></jl-pagination>
```

## Properties

Inputs: a JSX prop sets one, code calls `.set(value)` and `.get()`, HTML writes the attribute (lists and objects as JSON).

- `page` (attribute `page`): `number`, default `1`. The current page, from 1.
- `pages` (attribute `pages`): `number`, default `1`. How many pages there are.
- `siblings` (attribute `siblings`): `number`, default `1`. How many pages show on each side of the current one.
- `boundaries` (attribute `boundaries`): `number`, default `1`. How many pages always show at each end.
- `compact` (attribute `compact`): `boolean`, default `false`. Only the arrows and "3 of 12".
- `size` (attribute `size`): `'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'`, default `'md'`. The height of the buttons: 30, 36 or 44 pixels.
- `label` (attribute `label`): `string`, default `''`. The navigation’s name for screen readers, when a page has more than one. Empty: jlib's own text, in the language shown.

## Events

In JSX, the `on…` prop, its handler given the detail; in code, `events.register(name, (detail) => …)`. They do not bubble.

- `change` (`onChange` in JSX), detail `number`: People went to another page; the detail is its number, from 1.

## Styling

- `base` (part, `::part(base)`): The nav element around the buttons.

## Examples

HTML as the site renders it, with its layout classes (`row`, `stack`, `narrow`, `muted`), which are not jlib's: a view writes the same components by class in JSX. A script's `root` is the example's element.

### Near the ends, in the middle, and few pages

```html
<div class="stack">
  <jl-pagination pages="12" page="1"></jl-pagination>
  <jl-pagination pages="12" page="6"></jl-pagination>
  <jl-pagination pages="5" page="3"></jl-pagination>
</div>
```

### Siblings and boundaries

siblings="2" shows two pages on each side of the current one; boundaries="2" two at each end.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <jl-pagination pages="40" page="20" siblings="2"></jl-pagination>
  <jl-pagination pages="40" page="20" boundaries="2"></jl-pagination>
</div>
```

### Compact

Only the arrows and where people are.

```html
<div class="row">
  <jl-pagination compact pages="12" page="3"></jl-pagination>
  <jl-pagination compact size="sm" pages="4" page="1"></jl-pagination>
</div>
```

### Sizes

sm in dense tables, md by default, lg where a thumb presses it.

```html
<div class="stack">
  <jl-pagination size="sm" pages="10" page="4"></jl-pagination>
  <jl-pagination size="lg" pages="10" page="4"></jl-pagination>
</div>
```

### Paging results

Under a list: change says which page to load.

```html
<div class="stack narrow">
  <p class="muted demo-range">Showing 1–20 of 236 results</p>
  <jl-pagination class="demo-results" pages="12"></jl-pagination>
</div>
```

```js
const range = root.querySelector('.demo-range');
root.querySelector('jl-pagination').events.register('change', (page) => {
  const first = (page - 1) * 20 + 1;
  range.textContent = `Showing ${first}–${Math.min(first + 19, 236)} of 236 results`;
});
```
